tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate move legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before adding a move, check that the chosen disk is the topmost on its source peg and that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger. This guarantees that no size‑ordering or top‑disk violations occur.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Every time you generate a move, verify source‑top and destination‑top constraints.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 3 from a peg where disk 2 is on top, or moving disk 4 onto a peg whose top disk is disk 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use smallest disk as temporary buffer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be placed on any peg without breaking the size rule, so use it to occupy pegs temporarily and free larger disks for movement.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When a larger disk is blocked by a smaller one, move the smallest disk to another peg first.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Using disk 3 as a temporary buffer, which later blocks moving disk 2 because the smaller disk is no longer available.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat existing larger disks on target as base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the goal peg already contains some of the largest disks in the correct order, keep them untouched and build the rest of the tower on top of that partial stack.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the destination peg already holds a correctly ordered sub‑tower of larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving a correctly placed large disk (e.g., disk 5) off the goal peg, breaking the partial correct stack.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Iterative descending placement
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Place disks onto the goal peg in descending order (largest to smallest), moving each disk only after all larger disks are already correctly positioned.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When constructing the final tower, handle the next largest disk after the larger ones are in place.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to place disk 3 onto the goal peg before disk 4 is already there, resulting in an incorrect order.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final parseable list
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Ensure that the last syntactically correct list of moves in the response is the complete move sequence; avoid any trailing text that could be parsed as part of the list.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After generating the solution, place the move list as the very last element of the response.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Including explanatory text after the move list, causing the parser to stop at an incomplete list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Limit move list length to stay within token limits
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Generate a concise solution, preferably using the optimal or near‑optimal sequence of moves, so the total output fits within the token budget.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the move list starts to become long; look for shortcuts or combine moves to keep the output short.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Producing a 31‑move solution that exceeds the token limit, leading to truncation and an incomplete move list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Verify final configuration matches goal before outputting
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Mentally simulate each move from the initial configuration to ensure the final state exactly matches the goal configuration before publishing the move list.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After constructing the move list, double‑check the resulting tower against the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Assuming the final configuration is correct without checking, resulting in a mismatch between the final state and the goal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive sub‑tower transfer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move a stack of k disks from a source peg to a destination peg using the third peg, recursively move the top k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, move the largest disk, then move the k‑1 disks onto the destination.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need to relocate a contiguous sub‑tower of multiple disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move disks 3, 2, 1 as a single block instead of recursively moving the top two, then the largest, then the two again.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Avoid blocking future moves with temporary placements
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When using a disk as a temporary buffer, place it on a peg that will not need to be cleared for later moves of larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before moving a disk to a temporary peg, consider whether that peg will later need to be empty for a larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing the smallest disk on the same peg where a larger disk will later need to be moved, forcing extra shuffling.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear target peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk onto it
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a larger disk onto a peg, ensure the peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk; otherwise the move would violate the size rule.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you plan to place a larger disk onto a peg that currently holds smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 5 onto a peg whose top disk is disk 2.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may stop generation early or forget to include the move list after reasoning.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always produce a move list and place it as the final part of the response.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (size ordering violation)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may not check the destination peg's top disk before moving.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Validate move legality: ensure the destination top disk is larger or the peg is empty.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may lose track of which disk is on top of a peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Check that the chosen disk is the topmost on its source peg before moving.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may exceed token limits or stop generation prematurely.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Limit move list length and ensure the list is fully output before any other text.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a disk from a peg where it is not present
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may lose track of disk locations during multi‑step reasoning.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Maintain a mental (or written) representation of each peg's stack and update it after every move.
